identity.title: Thermal Physics of the Inner Coma: ALMA Studies of the Methanol Distribution and Excitation in Comet C/2012 K1 (PanSTARRS)

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present spatially and spectrally-resolved observations of CH$_3$OH emission from comet C/2012 K1 (PanSTARRS) using The Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) on 2014 June 28-29.

evidence.quote: while the comet was at a heliocentric distance $r_H=1.42$-1.43 AU and geocentric distance $\Delta=1.96$-1.97 AU

question.value: How do the CH3OH distribution, rotational temperature and excitation vary with distance from the nucleus in the inner coma of comet C/2012 K1 (PanSTARRS)?

evidence.quote: Two-dimensional maps of the line-of-sight average rotational temperature ($T_{rot}$) were derived, covering spatial scales $0.3''-1.8''$
It makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.01061.S.

bands.value: Band 6 (K=3-2 near 251.9 GHz) on June 28; Band 7 (J=7-6 near 338.5 GHz) on June 29

evidence.quote: The CH$_3$OH $K=3-2$ rotational band near 251.9 GHz (in ALMA receiver band 6) was observed on June 28 and the $J=7-6$ band near 338.5 GHz (in band 7) was observed on June 29.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: single 976 kHz spectral window per band, 488 kHz resolution (0.58 km/s Band 6, 0.43 km/s Band 7)

evidence.quote: in a single 976 kHz spectral window, using a spectral resolution of 488 kHz (0.58 km s$^{-1}$ in band 6 and 0.43 km s$^{-1}$ in band 7)
Forteen individual emission lines of the $K=3-2$ band were detected on 28 June
sixteen lines of the $J=7-6$ band were detected on 29 June
Thirty 12-m antennae, with baseline lengths 20-650 m
resulted in an angular resolution of $0.80''\times0.43''$ at 252 GHz and $0.71''\times0.33''$ at 338 GHz
the largest angular scale detectable in our observations is $\approx7.4''$ (or $\approx10^4$ km)

sensitivity.value: RMS per channel 1.8 mJy/beam (252 GHz), 3.0 mJy/beam (338 GHz)

evidence.quote: the measured RMS noise levels per channel were 1.8 mJy bm$^{-1}$ and 3.0 mJy bm$^{-1}$

time_on_source.value: 46 min at 252 GHz; 38 min at 338 GHz

evidence.quote: for a total of 46 min on-source at 252 GHz and 38 min on-source at 338 GHz

provided.value: OH 18 cm lines giving Q(OH) and water production rate

evidence.quote: The strengths of the 18 cm OH lines (at 1667 and 1665 MHz) in comet C/2012 K1 (PanSTARRS) were monitored using the Nançay radio telescope

angular resolution of $0.80''\times0.43''$ at 252 GHz and $0.71''\times0.33''$ at 338 GHz

The observational procedure and data analysis were described previously by (cite: cro02)

method.value: Average over 1.5'' circular aperture at the emission peak; integrate line ranges for maps

evidence.quote: These spectra were extracted by averaging the data over a circular aperture $1.5''$ in diameter, centered on the peak of the CH$_3$OH emission.

method.value: Rotational diagram at column density peak; integration limits ±1.5 km/s

evidence.quote: for our data, we used integration limits of $\pm1.5$ km s$^{-1}$ for all lines
Thus, we assumed equal abundances of $A$ and $E$ CH$_3$OH in our analysis from here on.

fitting.value: Linear fit to the diagram; errors from gradient and intercept

evidence.quote: Errors on $T_{rot}$ and $N$ were obtained from the errors on the gradient and intercept
are in good agreement with those obtained using the rotational diagram method

analysis_steps.goal: Spectral line fitting for Trot and N

method.value: Nonlinear least-squares fit of Gaussian optical depth curves per pixel, parameters Trot, N, FWHM

evidence.quote: fitting Gaussian optical depth curves to each emission line (as a function of frequency), parameterised by $T_{rot}$, $N$ and the line FWHM

key_parameters.value: Spectra smoothed by 3 km/s kernel; FWHM and Doppler shift held fixed

evidence.quote: allowing these values to be held fixed during the fitting

fitting.value: chi2 minimization; 300 Monte Carlo noise realizations, 1-sigma from ±68% percentiles

evidence.quote: 300 synthetic, Gaussian, random noise spectra were generated
with reduced $\chi^2$ values in the range 1.0-1.3

method.value: Pixel-by-pixel fit in 2''x2'' area; azimuthal averaging in 0.1'' annuli around column density peak; maps masked at >50% uncertainty

evidence.quote: our data were binned into a series of $0.1''$-wide annuli
These $\bar{S_{\nu}}(\rho)$ were subject to the same fitting procedure outlined in Section [4.3](#sec:modeling) to derive radial \[$T_{rot}$, $N$\] profiles

analysis_steps.goal: Haser model of column density and production rates

method.value: Haser outflow model run through CASA ALMA simulator and compared with N(rho)

evidence.quote: the model column density maps were run through the ALMA simulator in CASA with array configuration, imaging and cleaning parameters matching those of our observationions

assumptions.value: Constant outflow velocity 0.5 km/s, photodissociation rate 1e-5 s-1

evidence.quote: constant velocity of 0.5 km s$^{-1}$
provide an excellent fit to the observations on June 28, and a reasonably good fit on June 29

analysis_steps.goal: Non-LTE excitation modelling of Trot vs Tkin

method.value: Radiative transfer model of Biver et al. with collisions with H2O and electrons and solar pumping; trial Tkin(r) profiles

evidence.quote: A variety of different kinetic temperature profiles were tested in our radiative transfer model

key_parameters.value: Q(H2O)=1e29 s-1, v=0.5 km/s, cross section 5e-14 cm-2

evidence.quote: The H$_2$O production rate was taken to be $10^{29}$ s$^{-1}$ and outflow velocity 0.5 km s$^{-1}$
A variety of different kinetic temperature profiles were tested in our radiative transfer model, with the aim of reproducing the general behaviour of the observed $T_{rot}(r)$ profiles.
calibrated and cleaned using standard CASA routines (cite: cor14)
we obtain a water production rate of $(1.05\pm0.20)\times10^{29}$ s$^{-1}$
CH$_3$OH production rates of $1.9\times10^{27}$ s$^{-1}$ on June 28 and $1.4\times10^{27}$ s$^{-1}$ on June 29
with mixing ratios of 1.1-2.2%
decreased sharply from $116\pm18$ K to $42\pm4$ K between $\rho=0$-1000 km
followed by a relatively slow, steady decrease to $22\pm9$ K at $\rho=2500$ km

findings_qualitative.value: CH3OH column density profile consistent with isotropic uniform outflow from nucleus; no extended source

evidence.quote: no evidence is found for significant production of CH$_3$OH in the coma, either from icy grain sublimation or photochemistry

claims.hypothesis: Does coma Trot fall with distance beyond sub-thermal excitation?
claims.experiment: Line fitting of azimuthal spectra plus non-LTE modelling
claims.result: Observed Trot falls faster than for constant Tkin

evidence.quote: Sub-thermal excitation is therefore insufficient to fully explain the observed $T_{rot}$ behaviour in comet K1/PanSTARRS, and a variable $T_{kin}(r)$ profile is required.

claims.hypothesis: Is CH3OH released directly from the nucleus?

evidence.quote: these results imply that CH$_3$OH was sublimated directly from the nucleus of comet K1/PanSTARRS with mixing ratios of 1.1-2.2%.

claims.hypothesis: Do standard coma models explain the temperature drop?
claims.experiment: Compare with DSMC and multi-fluid models
claims.result: Observed drop less steep than models

evidence.quote: the observed temperature drop with distance is less steep than predicted by standard coma theoretical models

limitations_admitted.value: Elliptical beam and filtering limit interpretation; June 29 Trot profile hard to fit

evidence.quote: The elliptical shape of the telescope beam introduces some additional uncertainty into our radial temperature and column density profiles

referee_caveats_inferred: Tkin profiles chosen by eye without uncertainties
Two epochs only, different bands, so temporal comparison confounded by band excitation differences
